The warehouse team tracks inventory separately, HSE manually checks expiring certificates, and management struggles to see real-time site status. When a CSMS, ISO 45001, ISO 14001, ISO 9001, or SMK3 audit comes up, everyone ends up scrambling.
To solve this, I built a web-based ERP system that brings field operations and safety compliance into one clean dashboard:
🔹Warehouse & Logistics Tracks master inventory, inbound/outbound items, site asset mobilization, pending approvals, and automatic low-stock restock alerts.
🔹HSE & Compliance (ISO 45001, ISO 14001, ISO 9001 / SMK3 Ministry of Manpower Indonesia) Features a 30-Day Expiration & Calibration Radar to monitor employee Medical Check-Ups (MCU), equipment permits (SIO/SILO), tool calibrations, and PPE inspections—plus live tracking for open safety findings so nothing slips through the cracks.
🔹Admin & Audit Trail Includes role-based user access and full activity logs so every update is transparent and audit-ready at any time.
🔹Next Milestone: Project Budgeting & Cost Control (RAB / RAPP – In Progress) I am currently building theProject Cost Estimation & Execution Budget (RAB/RAPP) module to connect technical field operations directly with financial control.

 → Who handles payroll, BPJS contributions, and tax filings? Unclear.

This is where many global teams get stuck. The business is ready to grow. The legal structure isn't.

Hire full-time employees in Indonesia within days, not months. The EOR is the legal employer, handles contracts, payroll, benefits, and local compliance. You manage the work.

Already have an entity? Let a local expert handle monthly payroll, tax, and social security so your team doesn't have to learn Indonesian regulations the hard way.

Need ongoing HR support without building a full in-country team? Shared employment and HR services can fill the gap.

4. Test first, build later
Use EOR to validate the market, grow the team, then decide if (and when) to open your own entity. No upfront commitment, no sunk cost.
 
The truth is, expansion rarely fails because of the market. It fails because of slow, messy hiring infrastructure.
